Messages.Author: Daniel Figueiredo
Messages.Body:
Hi. I扉e been reading allthe posts on the new CAM set (like all of
you) for these past few days ans there is something that keeps nagging
me....

Why was it really necessary to change ALL the layout of the cards?
The new look is decidedly LESS "gothic-punk" or "gritty" or
"vampire-esque" than the old one. No discussion on that. To atract new
players WW says, and make it easier for them to recognize symbols and
play the game. But that is simply NOT the case I think. First of all,
VERY FEW new players, if any, will be playing the game exclusively
with new players, so when they play the game they will invariably see
the old cards, Jyhad cards, various variations of text on some
reprints (with more to come, if all the threads here are to be
beleived). In what way does that make it simpler for them? It does
not.

Imagine you are a new player, just bought a pair of CAM set
starters to play with your friend, you play a dozen times or so, think
you have the hang of it and go looking for other players to play with,
after all, this is a multiplayer game, best appreciated when more than
2 players participate. You find some new players, only to discover
that their cards are COMPLETELY different from yours! And suddenly,
for every 3 cards they use, 2 of them don愒 do what they say they do
in the text. How does that help? Well, it helps if you look
WAAAAAAAAAY into the future, after some 4 or more expansions with this
new look are released (I might still not be used to it then, having
played this game from day 1).

But if it is WW愀 intention to release much more expansions, then
they did not have to invent this new cript restriction. The Camarilla
will be "overpowered" by the huge influx of new vampires? Almost sure.
But this will be temporary, as vampires from other clans will
definately be released in the future (and not 10 years inthe future,
not even 2). So eventually, all clans would be balanced again. The
Camarilla was "overpowered" from the day it was released up until WW
released Sabbat Wars, and that did not ruin the game. On the contrary,
people fought and yelled and WW heard and brought the game back to
life.

Ah, but now we will have like 50 different princes and justicars!
Well, wou already could have that many just by electing them so. There
is a VERY good rule in this game that is called CONTESTING. Before no
one on the same game could have more than 1 prince of city X or
justicar of clan X. Now, no one on the same game can have more than
one prince of city X or justicar of clan X. Most cities won愒 even
have the same clan on their new princes if WW uses the "canon"
princes. Your cript is a fundamental part of your deck, but I think
this is giving it too much credit. The way the game stands you can
already make decent-to-great cripts of almost every clan. And beleive,
me a fantastic cript DOES NOT win you a game. I, and many people I
know have both won games with cripts built just for fun (like with one
of each vampire of clan X), and lost games with fully cusomised
cripts.

This all annoys me to no end... it doesn愒 do much more than that
because we can always ignore the little "3" and build whatever cript
we want (barring tournaments, of course). At least the clan
backgrounds could have remained the same, especially after the release
of bloodlines, with all those new looks. Now we get a dozen more. :(

So, why was this all necessary? Key word necessary. Maybe WW wants
the game to be fully thier own, and only by changing the look on the
cards can they get some sort of closure on this. It is a strange
decision they made. They must have known some people would fly off the
rocket in fury and rage. In the end these few poeple will either find
new and greener pastures to spend their money on or get used to it.
But I have the opinion that if you can avoid conflict of this sort,
why not? Keeping the clan backgrounds and card backgrounds, as well as
layout would have avoided 90% of this trouble. And in my opinion, kept
the game easier for new players to learn. If you say new players are
smart enough to get used to the new look along with the old, they
probably are. But it would be wrong to assume that they could not get
used to the old one. Since the old one contributes more to the "feel"
of the game, the old one being kept would entitle only one layout, and
the old one would even save WW some money by not having to create a
ton more card backgrounds. THese are all reasons why the old layout
alone is MUCH simpler to play with.

Well, my 2 cents.... (althoug they are currently worth less than half
a cent if you put then in dollars! :)

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Daniel Figueiredo wrote:
> But if it is WW愀 intention to release much more expansions, then
> they did not have to invent this new cript restriction. The Camarilla
> will be "overpowered" by the huge influx of new vampires? Almost sure.
> But this will be temporary, as vampires from other clans will
> definately be released in the future (and not 10 years inthe future,
> not even 2). So eventually, all clans would be balanced again.

No. Then all clans will be overpopulated.

The idea is to avoid custom crypts -

Custom Crypt: building a crypt first by imagining the
vampires you'd create to fill it, and then going to the
extensive ranks of actual vampires to find matches.

(As opposed to current: builing a crypt by pikcing an idea
and then finding vampires that best match that idea).

The game was designed with something else in mind.

Otherwise the rules would've been written with some sort of
point-cost vampire-construction rules to allow players to
Frankenstein the vampires that they wanted to be in their
crypts.

The game as it is was designed to have crypts built using
existing vampires (the group of which together failing to
represent any significant fraction of the set of all
possible vampires).

Messages.Author: jspektr
Messages.Body:
om...@uol.com.br (Daniel Figueiredo) wrote in message news:<b2fbf7ad.02070...@posting.google.com>...

> So, why was this all necessary? Key word necessary. Maybe WW wants
> the game to be fully thier own, and only by changing the look on the
> cards can they get some sort of closure on this. It is a strange
> decision they made. They must have known some people would fly off the
> rocket in fury and rage. In the end these few poeple will either find
> new and greener pastures to spend their money on or get used to it.

Yep. None of the visual design changes were necessary. At all. If they
wanted to make things easier to read, they could have done so while
keeping the basic layout and backgrounds the same. I think you might
be on to something with your "closure" theory.

In tech circles, this is known as the "not invented here" syndrome.
Companies refuse to use popular, established and reliable technology
because it was invented by someone else. So they make their own
version, but make it different, just to prove it is different, and
often make it less functional in the process.

I was speculating that the changes were made for business reasons, to
force players to stop buying old cards. But Daniel could be right. It
could simply boil down to the guys (and gals) at White Wolf wanted to
make the game their own. So they threw out the old design for one
completely different. If rumors are to be believed, many basic cards
are being changed, which will completely redefine game balance. It's
possible the reason isn't because the cards were broken at all, but
because White Wolf wants to make changes for the sake of changing
things, to show the world this is their game now and the old game is
gone.

Do I think any of this is true? Maybe. The staff at White Wolf has
their own reasons for doing this, and I expect we'll never know them.
But it's interesting to look at this and think about what might be
going on, and why.

JSpektr - btw, Brian Glass is the Art Director for VTES, and Aileen
Miles did the borders. Just in case anyone wondered.

Messages.Author: CurtAdams
Messages.Body:
om...@uol.com.br (Daniel Figueiredo) wrote in message
news:<b2fbf7ad.02070...@posting.google.com>...

> So, why was this all necessary? Key word necessary.

The new design highlights (in garish green) the most important
game aspects of the vampire-clan and disciplines. They sacked
off aesthetics for playability. If you don't think that's a good tradeoff
(I actually don't) that's your opinion but all these psychological
and conspiracy theories are just silly. They made a value decision
on what's important.

If you don't like the aesthetics, stick with your existing decks.
If you refuse to play because you think somebody else's deck
is unattractive then you'll have to refuse to play but I would think
CCGs would be very frustrating for somebody with those preferences.
I mean, I know a lot of people don't like Shy, but does anybody
actually get up and leave because somebody's playing BL?

Curt Adams (curt...@aol.com)

> The color green highlights the disciplines, making them much more

Easily done without the green bar. They still could have been made
larger and run down the side without changing any other aspect of the
card. They could have even gotten a white glow around each one to make
them stand out, and it would have been less jarring (and less ugly,
IMHO) than the green bar.

Again, the question was how does the green bar, by itself, do anything
that couldn't have been done with less alteration of the basic design?
It seems like change for change's sake to me. I've met a lot of
designers like that, once they are put in charge of a project someone
else has already done a good job on, they feel compelled to change it,
to leave their mark on it, even if it ultimately makes the design less
effective. Not that I'm saying that's what happened, just that it
seems like a possibility.

> new players. Clan background changes I can't explain, but maybe
> the art was owned by somebody besides WW and they're not willing
> to pay anymore.

If the current posts about reprinting Final Nights are true, then
reprinting the backgrounds must not be a problem. Unless they plan on
reprinting Final Nights in the new format.

JSpektr

Messages.Author: Geemarcus
Messages.Body:
First off hello all! This is my second post, but I realized I should
have said "hi" the first time. I've played the game since it was
Jyhad, but only seriously for about two years now.

Although I really hate the new card layout, I am willing to concede
that I may eventually get used to the green bar on the library cards,
and may even come to almost like it. Maybe. I think the thing that
really bothers me is the change to the Vampire cards. It was the
vampire cards that got me interested in the game in the first place.
They are almost portrait-like in nature, and the new format really
messes that up, making them look more like cards (which of course they
are, but you get what I mean...). Additionally, using the green bar
on both the library cards and the vampire cards makes them appear far
too similar. I won't get into the whole "difficult to tell apart"
because I've seen how people respond to that ("the have oval pictures
instead of square..."). At the very least, the bar used could have
been the same color as the amber crypt card backs, which would have
made a hell of a lot more sense, and wouldn't have been quite so
jarring.
